title: One Point Lesson - Gearbox Vibration Monitoring (VSHH-7802) (OPL-CT-7801-06)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-CT-7801-06 - Gearbox Vibration Monitoring (VSHH-7802).

Equipment: CT-7801 (COOLING TOWER CELL FAN), Discipline: Instrument, Area: 7800 - COOLING TOWER SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-7801 (SIL 1), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-7801.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains gearbox vibration monitoring (vshh-7802) for CT-7801 (COOLING TOWER CELL FAN) in the COOLING TOWER SYSTEM. A rising vibration trend warns of gear or bearing wear before the fan trips or throws a blade. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: De-energise and isolate the loop; place the function to bypass/inhibit under permit.
- Precaution 2: Inform the panel operator before working on any trip, valve or transmitter.
- Precaution 3: Take care with instrument air / hydraulic pressure when disconnecting tubing.
- Precaution 4: Verify intrinsic-safety / Ex integrity is restored before returning to service.
- Precaution 5: Wear correct PPE and follow ESD/override control procedures.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: HART communicator / positioner software (e.g. ValveLink)
- Tool 2: Loop calibrator & decade box / pressure source
- Tool 3: Digital multimeter and clamp meter
- Tool 4: Span/zero test gas or reference standards
- Tool 5: Torque screwdriver and small hand tools
- Tool 6: Certified test/inhibit permit

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Trend the VS-7802 reading on the PdM route
- Step 1 - Check: Loop isolated / under permit
- Step 2 - Action: Alarm at 6 mm/s and trip at 9 mm/s (VSHH-7802)
- Step 2 - Check: Reference standard traceable
- Step 3 - Action: Correlate the rise with gearbox oil temperature TE-7803
- Step 3 - Check: As-found & as-left recorded
- Step 4 - Action: Inspect the floating drive-shaft couplings
- Step 4 - Check: Trip / control action verified
- Step 5 - Action: Escalate a step-change to reliability
- Step 5 - Check: Return to service confirmed

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: Scheduled pH analyzer calibration | Likely Cause: Electrode drift | Action: Recalibrated AI-7805 on buffer solutions, replaced electrode
- Symptom: Blowdown conductivity reading unreliable | Likely Cause: Conductivity cell fouled with scale | Action: Cleaned and recalibrated AI-7806 conductivity cell
- Symptom: Routine barscreen cleaning on operator round | Likely Cause: Normal debris accumulation | Action: Raked barscreen clear, checked differential level

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: A rising vibration trend warns of gear or bearing wear before the fan trips or throws a blade.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-7801: e.g. VSHH-7802 trips at > 9 mm/s - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-7801 before working on CT-7801.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
